findings.cross_file_justification: endpoint_policy.py (full file) hop_is_local and _local_labels accept a provider-block `dispatch_group: local` (the entry inherits it when silent), and validate_providers admits an https endpoint on a loopback/RFC1918 host for such a provider with NO allow_insecure_endpoint. cheval.py _build_provider_config copies dispatch_group only from model_data (the model entry) into ModelConfig and sets allow_insecure_endpoint=None, so _transport_policy sees neither trigger and returns None.
findings.description: A provider declared local at the provider block (not on each model entry) over an https local endpoint is planned and admitted as a local hop by the loader (hop_is_local / _local_label_refusal), but the adapter builds no TransportPolicy for it: ModelConfig.dispatch_group is None (cheval only reads the model entry) and allow_insecure_endpoint is None (https on a local host needs no opt-in). The request then runs on the default transport: httpx trust_env=True honours HTTPS_PROXY/ALL_PROXY, and 3xx responses are followed by urllib. In addition, the endpoint_policy module docstring says the request-time half enforces the local-hop rule on the request host via `TransportPolicy.local`, but the TransportPolicy dataclass in base.py has no `local` field and check_url never applies local_host(); that half of D-8.1 is not implemented in this diff.
findings.failure_mode: Under hounfour.locality: local_voices a hop the planner treats as local can have its prompt sent to a proxy named in the environment, or to any host a 3xx from the local server points at, with no refusal and no record. The D-7.2 request-time rules (no proxy env, no redirects, path-prefix) silently do not apply to exactly the class of hop they exist for.
findings.suggested_fix: In cheval.py _build_provider_config resolve the effective group as `model_data.get("dispatch_group") or prov.get("dispatch_group")` before building ModelConfig (or better, call endpoint_policy.hop_is_local(config, provider_name, model_id) and store the result). In _transport_policy, treat `hop_is_local(...)` (or the resolved group) as the trigger alongside allow_insecure_endpoint. Add the `local: bool` field to TransportPolicy and, when set, require `local_host(r_host)` in check_url as the docstring promises. Add a test: provider-block dispatch_group local + https://127.0.0.1 endpoint, assert http_post_stream receives a policy.

findings.cross_file_justification: endpoint_policy.py hop_is_local is documented as 'ONE implementation for cheval's planner, the loader's fallback check and MODELINV hop_locality', and it honours a provider-block dispatch_group, excludes CLI hops, and requires the endpoint host to pass the local-hop rule. modelinv.py hop_locality_of reimplements the decision as `entry.get("dispatch_group") == "local"` on the model entry only, so the two disagree for provider-block declarations.
findings.description: hop_locality_of reads dispatch_group from the model entry only. A provider that declares `dispatch_group: local` at the provider block (accepted by validate_providers/_local_labels and treated as local by hop_is_local and the planner mirrors in hop-locality.py and Bridgebuilder isLocalVoice) is recorded as `hop_locality: hosted` on every MODELINV row. The audit chain therefore contradicts the plan and the loader for the same hop, and the documented single implementation (hop_is_local) is bypassed.
findings.failure_mode: Under local_voices, the MODELINV row for a locally-dispatched hop says hosted; anyone auditing locality from the chain (or counting local vs hosted spend) gets the wrong answer, and a hosted-vs-local discrepancy check between planner and audit will fire spuriously or miss real leaks.
findings.suggested_fix: Have hop_locality_of delegate: `from loa_cheval.config.endpoint_policy import hop_is_local; return "local" if hop_is_local(hounfour, provider, model_id) else "hosted"` (lazy import, as destination_for already does for split_url). Add a test with the provider-block form asserting hop_locality == "local".

findings.cross_file_justification: endpoint_policy.py (full file) defines validate_local_fallbacks for 'Audit a257-1 MEDIUM-A1 (b)': under locality local_voices a local model's fallback_chain to a hosted hop must be refused at load. validate_providers does not call it, and the loader.py diff adds only normalise_keyless and validate_providers. No other diff-touched file calls it.
findings.description: validate_local_fallbacks is defined and documented as a load-time refusal but is never invoked: validate_providers does not call it and load_config only calls normalise_keyless and validate_providers. The audit fix it implements is dead code. (If the working-tree loader already calls it and the diff shown is stale, dismiss; the diff and the escalated full file of endpoint_policy.py are visibly out of sync, so this should be checked explicitly.)
findings.failure_mode: Under hounfour.locality: local_voices a model with dispatch_group local and a fallback_chain naming a hosted alias loads cleanly; cheval walks that chain inside one call on a local-model failure and the prompt reaches a hosted provider, which is precisely the leak the audit finding described.
findings.suggested_fix: Call `validate_local_fallbacks(merged)` from load_config immediately after `validate_providers(merged)` (or from the end of validate_providers), and add a loader test: locality local_voices + local model whose fallback_chain names a hosted alias must raise ConfigError.

findings.description: hop_telemetry() returns destination/hop_locality only when the hop string contains ':' (provider:model). The completion emit feeds it `_modelinv_state["final_model_id"]`, then `models_failed[-1]["model"]`, then `models_requested[0]`. The models_failed records built in this same diff store `"model": _entry_target` with `"provider": _entry.provider` as a separate key, which indicates `_entry_target` (and very likely final_model_id, the resolved model id) are bare model ids without a provider prefix. For those values hop_telemetry silently returns only locality_mode, so the row carries no destination or hop_locality even though the comment and FR-7/FR-8 say every MODELINV row carries them. Verify the format of final_model_id; if it is `provider:model` this is moot for the success path, but the models_failed fallback is still bare.
findings.failure_mode: Successful (and last-tried-failed) completion rows lack `destination` and `hop_locality` under exactly the condition the fallback chain was written for, with no warning (the ':' guard returns before the try/except that logs). If the updated payload schema marks these fields required, the writer's schema validation would drop the row entirely.
findings.suggested_fix: Track the answering hop as `provider:model` in _modelinv_state (e.g. set `_modelinv_state["final_hop"] = f"{_entry.provider}:{_entry_target}"` where final_model_id is set, and record `"hop"` alongside `"model"`/`"provider"` in models_failed), and pass that to hop_telemetry. Alternatively, make hop_telemetry accept (provider, model_id) explicitly and log a warning when the hop cannot be split.

findings.description: The exit-7 (models_not_planned) MODELINV emit now evaluates `_preflight_head.canonical` as part of the kwargs. hop_telemetry itself is fail-soft, but the attribute access happens before it is called. If `_preflight_head` can be None on the path where no hop was planned (which is what exit 7 means), the AttributeError is swallowed by the surrounding fail-soft except and the whole exit-7 audit row is lost, not just the destination fields.
findings.failure_mode: No MODELINV row for the exit-7 refusal when the preflight head is absent; the printed fail-soft message is the only trace.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `getattr(_preflight_head, "canonical", None)` (hop_telemetry already handles None), or pass `_modelinv_models_requested[0]` as the fallback hop.

findings.description: The 400 heuristic matches any error body mentioning `response_format` or `json_schema`. OpenAI's strict-mode validation errors for schemas missing `additionalProperties: false` or non-exhaustive `required` read 'Invalid schema for response_format ...', so a server that fully supports response_format but rejects THIS schema is classified as 'server does not accept structured output' and the schema is silently dropped on the retry. Because `_build_chat_body` always sends `strict: true`, this will happen for most hand-written schemas on hosted OpenAI chat entries declaring structured_json. The retry costs little (400 precedes generation) and telemetry records schema_rejected_by_server, so this is a correctness/intent concern rather than a failure.
findings.failure_mode: Operators who declared structured_json to get enforcement receive unenforced output for ordinary schemas, with only a WARN log and a telemetry flag to tell them; the tolerant parser and repair loop then run on every such call.
findings.suggested_fix: Narrow the heuristic: treat as 'unsupported' only when the message indicates an unknown/unsupported parameter (e.g. contains 'unrecognized', 'unknown parameter', 'not supported', 'unsupported') and classify 'Invalid schema' messages as an InvalidInputError that surfaces the schema problem. Alternatively, drop `strict: true` unless the schema is strict-compatible, or document that strict compatibility is required.

findings.cross_file_justification: loader.py now calls validate_providers on every load_config; modelinv.py destination_for in the same diff performs a `{region}` substitution on provider endpoints, showing that templated endpoints like `https://bedrock-runtime.{region}.amazonaws.com` survive interpolation into the merged view.
findings.description: validate_providers runs validate_declared_endpoint on every non-CLI provider endpoint in the merged config. destination_for shows provider endpoints can still contain the literal `{region}` placeholder after interpolation. If the canonical validator refuses `{`/`}` in a host (most host-syntax checks do), config load now fails for any such provider even though it was previously loadable, and the failure is a hard ConfigError for every cheval invocation. test_config_examples_load.py may cover this if the shipped catalog contains a templated provider; if not, add a case.
findings.failure_mode: Every cheval command exits with a config error for a project that declares a region-templated provider endpoint.
findings.suggested_fix: In validate_providers substitute `region_default` (or a syntactically valid placeholder region) into `{region}` before calling check_endpoint, matching what destination_for does, and add a loader test with a templated endpoint.
